newsitem.title: GERMANY: German IG Metall unit seeks national sick pay deal.
newsitem.headline: German IG Metall unit seeks national sick pay deal.

text.p: A regional unit of Germany's largest union, IG Metall, said on Monday that it had given the labour group's executive board power to negotiate a deal on sick pay for the whole union at national level.
IG Metall's board went to the regions to get permission to continue the talks at the top level after failing to resolve a dispute with employers over planned sick pay cuts last week.

The dispute arose when firms started to implement a new law cutting sick pay to 80 percent of the normal wage from 100 percent currently without discussing this with the unions, causing a storm of worker protest.
Last week's talks broke up with the two sides so far apart that they could not even decide whether to talk further.

Union officials in Germany's most populous state, North Rhine-Westphalia, said after a meeting of the region's main wages commission that they had given the board permission to go ahead and negotiate on their behalf.

Responsibility for all pay negotiations routinely lies with the union's regional units and an employer wish that the sick pay issue be discussed along with the regular 1997 pay demand and other bonuses makes it doubly important for the board to secure the support of its officials in the regions.
But the regional unit, led by Harald Schartau, attached come conditions to its approval.

It warned that the union would go ahead with a planned day of action and protest on October 24 unless there were signs by October 23 that the union was closer to achieving its goal of retaining 100 percent sick pay.
IG Metall's board will notify the employer association Gesamtmetall as to whether it wants to continue talks on Friday. The talks would then be expected to resume next week.
